clue.text: Copy capital letters — it could be a revelation

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: something that could be a revelation is of that prophetic kind

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are taken and set out afresh, so 'letters' signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A scribe is told to copy out the capital letters of an important prophetic text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like part of 'capital letters' but signals that the eleven letters of COPY CAPITAL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocalypse is the biblical Book of Revelation, so a prophetic disclosure is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Low tide, but it's not very important

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, a very small amount of sea water, a tide at its lowest
an idiom for a contribution too small to matter

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is playful: a single drop of sea water is about as low a tide as you can get.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something trivially small compared with what is needed, hence unimportant.

clue.text: There's nothing bad about an oil producer

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for bad is read backwards

parts.note: bad means evil

explanation.surface: A claim that there is nothing harmful about an oil company.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive tree yields olive oil, so it is literally an oil producer.

clue.text: A friend embracing the queen after whom a country was named

definitions.text: after whom a country was named

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: amigo is Spanish for friend, also used in English
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A pal hugs the monarch, who gave her name to a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' belongs to the surface only; AMIGO already starts with A. Amerigo Vespucci is the explorer whose name gave America its name.
explanation.definitionFit: America takes its name from the Italian navigator Amerigo Vespucci, so his first name fits this description.

clue.text: Something worn out may shake endlessly

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their usual order
endlessly means the final letter of shake is dropped

explanation.surface: Something that has worn out may shake without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' takes E off SHAKE to leave SHAK; 'out' shuffles MAY plus SHAK. 'worn out' reads as one phrase, but 'worn' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women, so it is an item of clothing, something worn.

clue.text: Mark, a man of straw

definitions.meaning: Mark ..., son of the former British prime minister Margaret ...
literally a man who works with straw, roofing houses

explanation.walkthrough: 'a man of straw' normally means a weak person or a sham, but here it is literal: a roofer working in straw or reed.
explanation.definitionFit: A thatcher roofs buildings with straw or reed; Mark Thatcher is the son of Margaret Thatcher.

clue.text: V is like a funeral parlour

definitions.text: V is like a funeral parlour

parts.words: V is like a funeral parlour
parts.note: the letter V sits in the middle of the word gravity, and a funeral parlour is a place of solemn gravity, a hub of seriousness

explanation.walkthrough: Both readings share one phrase: V is literally the central letter of GRAVITY, and an undertaker's premises are a centre of gravity in the sense of solemnity.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics term for a balance point, here read as the middle of the word gravity and as a seat of solemnity.

clue.text: Van 3 feet off with little time — it's too late

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and need rearranging

parts.note: the numeral spelt out as a word
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A van has had three feet broken off, and with time short it is too late.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is just the number spelt out here, not a pointer to 3-down. 'off' signals the rearrangement, and T joins at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting after the event means acting once it is too late to make a difference.

clue.text: Introduction to children's literature?

parts.note: not a primer or course on children's books but the stock opening words of a fairy tale

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a course title; it actually means the words that begin so many children's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional opening formula of fairy tales, literally what introduces a children's story.

clue.text: To get a number in Smith's place is divine

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a blacksmith works at a forge
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's workshop gaining a numbered sign is somehow heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Pope's line 'To err is human, to forgive divine': the answer is what is divine in the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope's saying holds that pardoning others is a godlike act, the thing that is divine.

clue.text: Quiet girl on the river

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
Ann is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A silent young woman sits on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.

clue.text: Common PC device?

parts.note: PC means politically correct, not personal computer: a usual tactic of polite speech

explanation.walkthrough: PC suggests a computer gadget; here it is political correctness, whose standard device is a softened term.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild substitute for a blunt word, the stock tool of politically correct language.

clue.text: Some security is violated — damn!

indicators.note: violated means interfered with and wrecked, so the remaining letters are jumbled
only some of the word is used, so its last three letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A breach of security prompts an angry oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' keeps SECUR from SECURITY; 'is violated' rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of annoyance; 'Curse!' and 'Damn!' are interchangeable oaths.

clue.text: It's back to the city for almost nothing

indicators.note: back means the word it is turned round

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
NY stands for New York, the city par excellence

explanation.surface: Returning to the big city for next to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minute is so small it amounts to almost nothing.

clue.text: Poules ravished by chanticleer, which is fishy

parts.note: Chanticleer is the traditional name for a rooster, a cock

indicators.note: ravished means violently disturbed, so the letters of poules are jumbled

explanation.surface: Hens (French 'poules') are ravished by the farmyard rooster, which seems suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ravished' rearranges the French word for hens into LE SOUP. 'fishy' looks like it means suspicious, but here it is literal: a soup made with shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockles are small edible shellfish, so a soup made from them is literally fishy.

clue.text: English getting on, but attractive

parts.note: getting on means growing old, ageing

explanation.surface: An elderly Englishman who is nonetheless charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming or appealing, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: English church, one without a clue, all at sea

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
having no idea means being without a clue

explanation.surface: An English churchman who is hopelessly confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' looks like the bewildered churchman again, but it is literal: Echinoidea is the class of sea urchins, which live only in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinoidea, the sea urchins, are a marine class of animals, so they are all at sea.

clue.text: Understanding of Scots household goods

definitions.meaning: perception or grasp of a matter
in Scots dialect the word means household furniture and goods

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is an old Scots word for the contents of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means deep understanding, and in Scots also the furnishings of a household.

clue.text: Student at university beset by rising din finds a way out

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: din means noise
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: A student on campus, surrounded by growing noise, finds an escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NOISE into ESION; 'beset by' puts L and U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elusion is the act of escaping or evading, so it provides a way out.

clue.text: Not in favour of having a drink

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to having a tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: AGIN is a dialect form of 'against'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect variant of against, meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Shakespearean instrument

definitions.meaning: a Shakespeare character, the heroine of Twelfth Night
a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests an Elizabethan instrument, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night and also the alto member of the violin family.

clue.text: 4 teas said to be laced with sugar in Germany

indicators.note: laced with means threaded through, so the letters are mixed together
said means the word teas is heard rather than spelt, giving the letter T four times

parts.note: four cups of tea: the word teas spoken four times sounds like four letter Ts
taken as written

explanation.surface: Four cups of tea, sweetened with sugar, served somewhere in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns 4 teas into TTTT, and 'laced with' threads them through SUGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuttgart is a major city in south-west Germany, capital of Baden-Wurttemberg.

clue.text: Actress, the last of 3

definitions.meaning: in a sequence of three items, the final one

explanation.walkthrough: Dame Thora Hird was a much-loved British comic actress; with her initial the name gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal for the final item of three, and the initial and surname of the actress Thora Hird.

clue.text: Short causing dead engine

indicators.note: causing means producing something new out of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A short circuit has killed the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' rearranges D and ENGINE. 'Short' reads as an electrical fault, but it means lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be short of something is to be lacking or in want of it.

clue.text: Old city free for student element

indicators.note: for means one piece is swapped in place of the other

parts.note: Ilium is the Latin name of Troy, the ancient city
L is a learner, a student
rid means to free

explanation.surface: An ancient city made free to a student.
explanation.walkthrough: RID replaces the L in ILIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridium is a dense metallic chemical element of the platinum group.

clue.text: Song, or anything Dad murdered round the clock

indicators.note: murdered means mangled, as a song can be murdered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone's father is butchering a song at all hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'murdered' rearranges ANYTHING DAD. 'Song' is an extra pointer: Night and Day is a Cole Porter song.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means continually, all the time, as does round the clock.
